bull_bear.body: Quintype’s operating control shift on Oct 1, 2025, will instantly add ~300M+ monthly page views and SaaS revenue to consolidated statements — a hidden catalyst not reflected in FY25 results; Kisan India (ex-Quint Hindi) YouTube channel is now a standalone asset under Shvaas Creations
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Digital-native, AI-focused positioning: described as India's leading digital and media-tech, AI-focused company, with The Quint operating since 2015
- Platform scale in media-tech: Quintype's AI-assisted publishing platform serves 300+ publishers globally and manages over a billion monthly pageviews, with content produced in as many as 25 languages
- Marquee publisher and enterprise client base - BQ Prime, The Quint, Fortune India, Karjalainen and I-Mediat on Quintype; Spotify, Amazon, Disney and Lionsgate on ListenFirst
- Multi-brand portfolio addressing distinct audiences - English national news, Southern India regional news, youth citizen media and agriculture - allowing separate positioning within one digital ecosystem
- Integrated stack combining content, publishing technology and AI-driven social media analytics, which the Company positions as an end-to-end capability for publishers and brands
- Exclusive India franchise relationship with Time Out Group plc covering both Time Out Media and Time Out Market
- Concentrated promoter ownership - the promoter holds 62.57% of Quint Digital Limited
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data privacy and cyber security — The only BRSR material issue the Company classifies as a Risk with negative financial implications. As a digital platform, a breach can compromise customer information and the Company's content; mitigation is a strict IT policy adhered to at all times plus a dedicated IT team constantly monitoring security processes.
- Thinning margins across the media industry — Listed first under Threats in the MD&A Opportunities and Threats section - media companies are witnessing revenue drops (the disclosure is truncated in the routed text), and the Company competes in ad-supported niches where competition is explicitly acknowledged.
- Heavy export / overseas revenue concentration — Exports contributed 78.86% of the entity's total turnover per BRSR Section A, so the bulk of income depends on overseas clients and geographies (principally the US media-tech business), exposing the Company to foreign-currency and offshore-demand shifts.
- Single-activity revenue concentration — BRSR discloses that 90% of turnover comes from a single main activity - other information and communication service activities, specifically operation of websites acting as internet portals with periodically updated content - leaving little revenue diversification within the listed entity.
- Talent dependence and employee attrition — The business is people-led (content, editorial and engineering). Permanent-employee turnover was 21.79% in FY 2025-2026, an improvement on 55.72% in FY 2024-2025 and 42.96% in FY 2023-2024, but historically elevated attrition remains a structural exposure.
- Energy and infrastructure dependence — BRSR states that as a digital company the core asset is the hardware and infrastructure that powers The Quint, and the Company heavily depends on energy to maintain operations; it is framed as an opportunity to be addressed through energy-efficient equipment, but the underlying dependence is structural.
- Structural disruption of the media and entertainment business model — The MD&A notes monetization is shifting from linear TV to digital, that legacy players are restructuring portfolios and spinning off digital-first entities, and that over 50 players are consolidating around high-value original content - management explicitly recognises disruption as a fundamental architecture of the M&E sector requiring agility and continuous reinvention.
- Execution risk on diversification beyond digital media — The Company amended its object clause to enter hospitality and food services, cultural and experiential ventures and real estate, and signed a sub-lease for the first Time Out Market in Delhi - businesses materially different in operating model from its asset-light digital media and media-tech base.
- Reputational risk around journalistic integrity and misinformation — BRSR identifies journalistic integrity and transparency in reporting as a material issue central to the Company's credibility; the entire owned-media franchise depends on being seen as a credible and transparent media source.

business.body: QDL operates a portfolio of digital news and content platforms - The Quint (English news and views, launched 2015), The News Minute (independent journalism from Southern India), Youth Ki Awaaz (citizen media) and Kisan India (Indian agriculture) - reaching audiences through websites, YouTube channels and social platforms. Alongside the media business it sells media technology: Quintype Technologies India Limited provides an AI-powered digital publishing SaaS platform used by 300+ publishers worldwide, while Quintype Technologies Inc. (US) operates the ListenFirst platform, which supplies social media analytics and digital intelligence to enterprises and brands. During FY26 the Company entered lifestyle, commerce and experiential retail through a franchise arrangement with Time Out Group for Time Out Media and Time Out Market in India.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Media-tech remains the declared long-term focal area even as the Company diversifies - the Founder states that QDL's focal area remains media-tech as part of the long-term strategy
- Strategic diversification into hospitality and lifestyle through an exclusive franchise agreement with Time Out Group, UK, to launch Time Out India as a digital city guide and to develop the first Time Out India Market in Delhi, creating a new content niche and revenue stream
- Continued strategic and portfolio investments in emerging and high-potential businesses, including raising the stake in NASDAQ-listed Lee Enterprises Inc. to 14.59% to expand further into the US market
- Strengthening the financial position by reducing borrowings and finance costs so as to free capacity to expand into and grow new business areas
- Building AI-led media technology for publishers - Quintype's Bold CMS with SAGE AI, Metype audience engagement, Quintype Ahead no-code website/app builder and Accesstype paywall/subscription management - to help publishers create, distribute and monetize content and improve their margins
- Integrating ListenFirst into Quintype Technologies Inc. to combine content analytics with strategic marketing insight and deliver end-to-end digital transformation solutions with a strong North American presence
- Continuing to operate and grow the owned digital platforms - The Quint, The News Minute, Kisan India and Youth Ki Awaaz - on original, high-quality journalism, enterprise journalism, ground reports and fact checks
- Converting industry disruption into leadership by adopting convergence of conventional channels and digital streaming, data-led decision making and experiential formats, and by staying agile, purposely innovative and collaborative
- Energy management identified as a material BRSR issue with positive financial implications - the Company intends to significantly reduce energy consumption and associated costs by adopting energy-efficient equipment for the hardware and infrastructure that powers its platforms
- Data privacy and cyber security governed by a strict IT policy adhered to at all times, supported by a robust IT team that constantly monitors security processes, with a published IT Policy under NGRBC Principle 9
- Diversity, equity and inclusion for employees treated as a material issue, with employee-friendly policies aimed at better engagement and productivity; women constitute 44.44% of the Board of Directors and 33.33% of Key Management Personnel
- Diversity, equity and inclusion in media representation described as core to the editorial philosophy - being a platform for marginalised voices and bringing stories from India's most remote corners
- Journalistic integrity and transparency in reporting maintained through an inclusive and bipartisan approach and platforms to debunk misinformation
- Board-approved policies covering all nine NGRBC principles and their core elements, published on the Company website; policies have been translated into procedures for eight of the nine principles (not for Principle 8)
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for every stakeholder group - communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value-chain partners - backed by a published Grievance Redressal Policy and a Whistle Blower Policy
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, with a published CSR Policy
- BRSR disclosures are made on a standalone basis, and no external assurance provider has been appointed and no assurance obtained on the report
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: QDL is an asset-light digital business; the routed sections disclose no plants, capacity additions or commissioning schedules, and expansion is described entirely as new verticals, corporate structure and platform footprint. The single largest expansion step is the move into lifestyle, food and experiential retail. To enable it, the Board on May 27, 2025 and the Members at the 40th AGM on September 16, 2025 approved altering the Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association to add hospitality and food services (ownership, management and operation of hotels, resorts, restaurants, cafes, food courts and entertainment services), cultural and experiential ventures (curated food halls, gastronomic hubs, beverage venues, performance spaces and brand engagement platforms) and real estate activities including acquisition, development, leasing and management of immovable properties; the Registrar of Companies, Delhi approved the alteration by certificate dated October 3, 2025. On the same May 27, 2025 date the Company signed two agreements with Time Out Group - a Master Franchise Agreement with Time Out Market Limited for launching Time Out Media in India as a digital destination with locally curated editorial content, and a Time Out Franchise Agreement with Time Out England Limited for developing Time Out Market opportunities in India as an immersive food and cultural destination. Physical build-out began with a Sub-Lease Agreement dated February 9, 2026 with Alborz Developers Limited for setting up the first Time Out Market in Delhi, and on April 24, 2026 the Company formally launched Time Out India and announced its first Time Out Market in New Delhi. Structurally, under the Amended and Restated Stockholders' Agreement dated August 29, 2025 with Cognita Ventures LLC, wholly owned subsidiary Global Media Technologies Inc. acquired majority control over the Board of Quintype Technologies Inc.; with GMT holding a 50% shareholding and board control, QT Inc. and its subsidiary Quintype Services India Private Limited became material subsidiaries with effect from October 1, 2025, having previously been joint ventures - deepening the Company's US media-tech footprint. To fund this expansion the Board on January 30, 2026 and the Members by Postal Ballot dated March 5, 2026 approved reclassifying the authorised share capital to create a preference-share class, and the Board considered an additional investment in Lee Enterprises Inc. at its meeting on December 30, 2025 (the disclosure is truncated in the routed text). Earlier footprint additions referenced include a 77.5% stake in Shvaas Creations, which runs the Kisan India agriculture YouTube channel.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Digital media crossed INR 1 trillion for the first time with 30.5% growth and became the largest segment in the Indian M&E industry, a segment the Company describes itself as a pure-play participant in
- Digital advertising surged 26% to reach INR 947 billion, making 63% of total ad revenues, with SME and long-tail advertisers accounting for 41% of digital ad revenue - the Company says it operates in different niches and is poised to attract audiences and advertisers
- Digital subscription revenues surged 60% as paid premium sports, films, video and music subscriptions expanded
- Digital media momentum has triggered the demand for media-tech and digital intelligence to scale and sustain in this space - the stated demand driver for Quintype and ListenFirst
- Publishers are shifting from traffic-led models to trust-based, loyalty-driven ecosystems built on subscriptions, communities, memberships and branded content, which management says QDL's media-tech can help scale
- Linear TV is expected to lose viewers to Connected TVs on the back of broadband push by cable operators and telcos, a shift management says the Company stands to gain from as a pure-play digital media player
- Rising accessibility - telecom subscriptions of 1.23 billion, 5G subscriptions up 39% to 395 million, broadband users crossing 1 billion, 584 million smartphone users spending 5.4 hours per day - broadening the addressable digital audience and driving multi-language consumption
- AI is enabling creation, personalization, monetization and scaling of content, and media players are increasingly using audience data for performance advertising with measurable ROI
- Out-of-home and experiential formats are expanding with city infrastructure and digital screens, which management says QDL's media-tech, media analytics and audience engagement can serve
- Management states the subsidiaries Quintype Technologies India Limited and Quintype Technologies Inc. contributed significantly to the Company's top and bottom lines and are anticipated to continue the same in future
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

currentContext.expansion: QDL is an asset-light digital business; the routed sections disclose no plants, capacity additions or commissioning schedules, and expansion is described entirely as new verticals, corporate structure and platform footprint. The single largest expansion step is the move into lifestyle, food and experiential retail. To enable it, the Board on May 27, 2025 and the Members at the 40th AGM on September 16, 2025 approved altering the Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association to add hospitality and food services (ownership, management and operation of hotels, resorts, restaurants, cafes, food courts and entertainment services), cultural and experiential ventures (curated food halls, gastronomic hubs, beverage venues, performance spaces and brand engagement platforms) and real estate activities including acquisition, development, leasing and management of immovable properties; the Registrar of Companies, Delhi approved the alteration by certificate dated October 3, 2025. On the same May 27, 2025 date the Company signed two agreements with Time Out Group - a Master Franchise Agreement with Time Out Market Limited for launching Time Out Media in India as a digital destination with locally curated editorial content, and a Time Out Franchise Agreement with Time Out England Limited for developing Time Out Market opportunities in India as an immersive food and cultural destination. Physical build-out began with a Sub-Lease Agreement dated February 9, 2026 with Alborz Developers Limited for setting up the first Time Out Market in Delhi, and on April 24, 2026 the Company formally launched Time Out India and announced its first Time Out Market in New Delhi. Structurally, under the Amended and Restated Stockholders' Agreement dated August 29, 2025 with Cognita Ventures LLC, wholly owned subsidiary Global Media Technologies Inc. acquired majority control over the Board of Quintype Technologies Inc.; with GMT holding a 50% shareholding and board control, QT Inc. and its subsidiary Quintype Services India Private Limited became material subsidiaries with effect from October 1, 2025, having previously been joint ventures - deepening the Company's US media-tech footprint. To fund this expansion the Board on January 30, 2026 and the Members by Postal Ballot dated March 5, 2026 approved reclassifying the authorised share capital to create a preference-share class, and the Board considered an additional investment in Lee Enterprises Inc. at its meeting on December 30, 2025 (the disclosure is truncated in the routed text). Earlier footprint additions referenced include a 77.5% stake in Shvaas Creations, which runs the Kisan India agriculture YouTube channel.

risks.note: The only BRSR material issue the Company classifies as a Risk with negative financial implications. As a digital platform, a breach can compromise customer information and the Company's content; mitigation is a strict IT policy adhered to at all times plus a dedicated IT team constantly monitoring security processes.

risks.risk: Thinning margins across the media industry
risks.note: Listed first under Threats in the MD&A Opportunities and Threats section - media companies are witnessing revenue drops (the disclosure is truncated in the routed text), and the Company competes in ad-supported niches where competition is explicitly acknowledged.

Exports contributed 78.86% of the entity's total turnover per BRSR Section A, so the bulk of income depends on overseas clients and geographies (principally the US media-tech business), exposing the Company to foreign-currency and offshore-demand shifts.

BRSR discloses that 90% of turnover comes from a single main activity - other information and communication service activities, specifically operation of websites acting as internet portals with periodically updated content - leaving little revenue diversification within the listed entity.

The business is people-led (content, editorial and engineering). Permanent-employee turnover was 21.79% in FY 2025-2026, an improvement on 55.72% in FY 2024-2025 and 42.96% in FY 2023-2024, but historically elevated attrition remains a structural exposure.

BRSR states that as a digital company the core asset is the hardware and infrastructure that powers The Quint, and the Company heavily depends on energy to maintain operations; it is framed as an opportunity to be addressed through energy-efficient equipment, but the underlying dependence is structural.

risks.risk: Structural disruption of the media and entertainment business model
risks.note: The MD&A notes monetization is shifting from linear TV to digital, that legacy players are restructuring portfolios and spinning off digital-first entities, and that over 50 players are consolidating around high-value original content - management explicitly recognises disruption as a fundamental architecture of the M&E sector requiring agility and continuous reinvention.

risks.risk: Execution risk on diversification beyond digital media
risks.note: The Company amended its object clause to enter hospitality and food services, cultural and experiential ventures and real estate, and signed a sub-lease for the first Time Out Market in Delhi - businesses materially different in operating model from its asset-light digital media and media-tech base.

risks.risk: Reputational risk around journalistic integrity and misinformation
risks.note: BRSR identifies journalistic integrity and transparency in reporting as a material issue central to the Company's credibility; the entire owned-media franchise depends on being seen as a credible and transparent media source.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Quint Digital Limited is a BSE-listed, digital-native Indian media and media-tech group that pairs owned digital news brands with an AI-powered publishing platform for global publishers and a social-media analytics platform for enterprises, and is now extending into lifestyle and experiential …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: QDL operates a portfolio of digital news and content platforms - The Quint (English news and views, launched 2015), The News Minute (independent journalism from Southern India), Youth Ki Awaaz (citizen media) and Kisan India (Indian agriculture) - reaching audiences through websites, YouTube channels and social platforms. Alongside the media business it sells media technology: Quintype Technologies India Limited provides an AI-powered digital publishing SaaS platform used by 300+ publishers worldwide, while Quintype Technologies Inc. (US) operates the ListenFirst platform, which supplies social media analytics and digital intelligence to enterprises and brands. During FY26 the Company entered lifestyle, commerce and experiential retail through a franchise arrangement with Time Out Group for Time Out Media and Time Out Market in India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Digital media crossed INR 1 trillion for the first time with 30.5% growth and became the largest segment in the Indian M&E industry, a segment the Company describes itself as a pure-play participant in
- Digital advertising surged 26% to reach INR 947 billion, making 63% of total ad revenues, with SME and long-tail advertisers accounting for 41% of digital ad revenue - the Company says it operates in different niches and is poised to attract audiences and advertisers
- Digital subscription revenues surged 60% as paid premium sports, films, video and music subscriptions expanded
- Digital media momentum has triggered the demand for media-tech and digital intelligence to scale and sustain in this space - the stated demand driver for Quintype and ListenFirst
- Publishers are shifting from traffic-led models to trust-based, loyalty-driven ecosystems built on subscriptions, communities, memberships and branded content, which management says QDL's media-tech can help scale
- Linear TV is expected to lose viewers to Connected TVs on the back of broadband push by cable operators and telcos, a shift management says the Company stands to gain from as a pure-play digital media player
- Rising accessibility - telecom subscriptions of 1.23 billion, 5G subscriptions up 39% to 395 million, broadband users crossing 1 billion, 584 million smartphone users spending 5.4 hours per day - broadening the addressable digital audience and driving multi-language consumption
- AI is enabling creation, personalization, monetization and scaling of content, and media players are increasingly using audience data for performance advertising with measurable ROI
- Out-of-home and experiential formats are expanding with city infrastructure and digital screens, which management says QDL's media-tech, media analytics and audience engagement can serve
- Management states the subsidiaries Quintype Technologies India Limited and Quintype Technologies Inc. contributed significantly to the Company's top and bottom lines and are anticipated to continue the same in future
